requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall develop, maintain, and execute a Software Development Plan and a Software Security Plan covering the full software life cycle from requirements through retirement, addressing every applicable requirement of NPR 7150.2D per the approved Requirements Mapping Matrix.
rationale: Requires development, maintenance, and execution of life-cycle software and security plans addressing applicable NPR obligations through the approved mapping matrix.

requirement_text: The NASA software shall meet performance expectations as determined by the development team prior to delivery.
rationale: Performance expectations do not require the project manager to define and document software acceptance criteria.

requirement_text: For Class B software, the NASA Project Manager shall perform, record, and maintain bidirectional traceability between higher-level and software requirements, software requirements and system hazards, software requirements and design components, design components and code, software requirements and software verifications, and software requirements and software non-conformances. The traceability records shall be updated within five business days of a requirement change.
rationale: Covers every Class B relationship in Table 1, including hazards and non-conformances.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall establish, capture, record, approve, and maintain software requirements, including requirements for the reused GPS ephemeris library, in the DOORS requirements repository as part of the project technical specification.
rationale: Requires every listed requirements-management action and makes the technical-specification role explicit.

requirement_text: Changes to NASA software requirements shall be logged in the issue tracker by the engineer making the change.
gap_type: Missing obligation to manage requirement changes
rationale: Logging requirement changes provides recording and tracking, but no obligation to manage them. The cited clause does not itself mandate a CCB or a particular approval procedure.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall perform requirements validation with the customer, including scenario-based walkthroughs and a requirements review board, to confirm the software will perform as intended in the lunar relay operational environment prior to baselining.
rationale: Requires requirements validation demonstrating intended behavior in the customer operational environment.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall transform the approved software requirements into a recorded software architecture, documented in the Software Architecture Description Document (SADD) and baselined under configuration management prior to detailed design.
rationale: Requires transformation of software requirements into a recorded architecture.

requirement_text: NASA software developers shall write clean, maintainable code following good engineering judgment.
rationale: Clean code and engineering judgment do not select, define, or commit adherence to software coding methods, standards, and criteria.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall use static analysis tools during development and testing to analyze code for defects, software security, code coverage, and software complexity, and shall track identified findings to closure in the defect tracking system.
rationale: Includes both phases and all four minimum analysis purposes in the clause.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall unit test each software code unit against its detailed design prior to integration, and shall record unit test results in the test management system.
rationale: Requires software code unit testing; recorded results and timing add detail beyond SWE-062.

requirement_text: NASA unit tests shall be executed by the responsible developer during code review.
rationale: Requires test execution but supplies no repeatability assurance. SWE-186 does not require automation specifically, so the rationale should focus on missing repeatability rather than missing automation.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall test the flight and ground software against its baselined software requirements, using documented test procedures and pass/fail criteria traceable to each requirement.
rationale: Requires software testing against requirements.

requirement_text: NASA software items may be placed under configuration management once qualification testing has demonstrated stable behavior.
gap_type: CM baseline established after testing, not before
rationale: Makes configuration management optional after qualification testing without requiring placement before testing.

requirement_text: For safety-critical NASA flight software components, the Project Manager shall achieve high structural test coverage as demonstrated by the test team.
gap_type: Coverage target not quantified to the required standard
rationale: Positively requires structural test coverage for safety-critical components but omits 100 percent and MC/DC. The source note allows deviations through technical authority review and waiver; it does not make an unspecified alternate standard automatically sufficient.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall verify through test every software requirement that traces to a hazardous event, hazard cause, or hazard mitigation technique in the NASA Hazard Analysis, and shall record the verification evidence in the Verification Compliance Matrix.
rationale: Includes hazardous events, causes, and mitigation techniques, with verification through test.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall perform a software cybersecurity assessment of all flight and ground software components under Agency security policies and project cybersecurity requirements, including risks posed by COTS, GOTS, MOTS, open-source, and reused software components, before Critical Design Review.
rationale: Includes Agency policy, project requirements, and risks from third-party or reused software.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall test the software cybersecurity mitigations identified in the Cybersecurity Risk Register.
rationale: Requires testing of cybersecurity mitigations but omits recorded results and does not establish vulnerability/weakness-analysis provenance of the register.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall identify, record, and implement secure coding practices (e.g., input validation, least privilege, secure error handling) in the Secure Coding Standard, and shall verify adherence during code review.
rationale: Requires identification, recording, and implementation of secure coding practices.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall develop a Software Configuration Management Plan describing the functions, responsibilities, and authority for configuration management activities across the software life cycle, including the composition and authority of the Configuration Control Board.
rationale: Requires a CM plan describing functions, responsibilities, and authority.

requirement_text: The NASA Configuration Control Board may perform software configuration audits at its discretion.
gap_type: Audits are optional rather than performed
rationale: Discretionary audits do not impose the mandatory configuration-audit activity or its required checks.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall perform and report software peer reviews or inspections for software requirements; software plans, including cybersecurity plans; design items identified for review in the software development plans; software code defined for review in the software or project plans; and software test procedures. Findings shall be recorded in the peer review log.
rationale: Covers all five artifact categories in items a through e, with both performance and reporting.

requirement_text: NASA software management and technical measurements shall be collected by each subsystem lead and stored in a shared spreadsheet.
gap_type: No reporting, maintenance, or utilization of measurements
rationale: Collection and spreadsheet storage cover some measurement activity, but no obligation to maintain, report, or utilize the measurements is present.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall track and maintain all software non-conformances, including defects found in ground support tools and reused software components, in the Non-Conformance Tracking System through closure.
rationale: Requires tracking and maintaining all software nonconformances through closure; ground support tools are explicitly included.

requirement_text: NASA software non-conformances shall be assigned by the reporting engineer to severity level 'important' or 'not important'.
rationale: Implements categories but leaves their severity criteria undefined; the clause requires clear levels.

requirement_text: Before acquiring or using the reused GPS ephemeris library or COTS RTOS, the NASA Project Manager shall identify the requirements each component must meet; obtain documentation sufficient for its intended purpose; address rights, licenses, ownership, warranty, transfer, and conditions of use with Center Intellectual Property Counsel; plan adequate future support; verify and validate each component to the same level as comparable developed software; and plan periodic assessments of vendor-reported defects for project impact.
rationale: Explicitly covers all six conditions without naming the expected SWE ID inside the example.

requirement_text: The project manager shall document that the spacecraft navigation software team’s progress will be reviewed and audited at the design-completion and testing-completion milestones.
rationale: Defines documented milestones for developer progress review and audit.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall collect the number of changes to the spacecraft navigation software requirements each month, track those changes in a requirements log, and report the results to the project team at monthly reviews.
rationale: Requires collecting, tracking, and reporting the count of requirement changes, a volatility metric.

requirement_text: The project manager shall provide NASA with a PDF containing screenshots of the spacecraft navigation software’s source code at project completion.
gap_type: Source code not provided in a modifiable format
rationale: Screenshots do not give NASA electronic source code in a modifiable format.

requirement_text: For every high-severity software non-conformance, the NASA Project Manager shall assess the software processes that contributed to the defect and implement a closed-loop corrective-action process that tracks process improvements through resolution.
rationale: Explicitly assesses contributing processes and closes corrective actions for every high-severity case.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall require the spacecraft navigation software developers to provide NASA with software products, requirements traceability, change records, defect reports, and development and management metrics in electronic format.
rationale: Requires electronic software products, traceability, change information, nonconformances, and development/management metrics.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall record the spacecraft navigation software’s size and effort estimates, milestones, and project characteristics in the team’s internal planning document at each major milestone.
gap_type: Missing submission to Center measurement repository
rationale: Requires the planning parameters at major milestones but only records them internally, omitting submission to the Center measurement repository.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall require the spacecraft navigation software developers to provide a software development schedule for NASA’s review and submit updated schedules whenever NASA requests them.
rationale: Requires a developer schedule for project review and requested updates.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall hold monthly meetings with project stakeholders to review the spacecraft navigation software’s schedule, development activities, performance metrics, and assessment results.
rationale: Requires regular stakeholder reviews of schedule, activities, metrics, and assessments but omits tracking issues to resolution.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall conduct regression testing after changes to the spacecraft navigation software to confirm that previously working features still function correctly.
rationale: Requires regression testing for preserved functionality but omits planning and a demonstration that changes did not introduce security vulnerabilities.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall plan and track project-specific software training for all project personnel and ensure that each person completes the training needed for their project work.
rationale: Plans, tracks, and ensures project-specific training across the stated project-personnel scope.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall document the conditions the spacecraft navigation software must meet before NASA accepts it.
rationale: Documenting the conditions for acceptance reasonably entails defining and documenting acceptance criteria.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall record problems found in the spacecraft navigation software in a defect log when they are first reported.
gap_type: Missing ongoing maintenance of problem records
rationale: Initial defect logging supplies records but not ongoing tracking and maintenance or explicit applicable tools/ground-software scope.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall define clear severity levels and their assignment criteria, and implement those levels for all software non-conformances in the spacecraft navigation system, including tools, COTS, GOTS, MOTS, open-source and reused components, and applicable ground systems.
rationale: Defines clear criteria and implements levels across every listed applicable component category.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall record and maintain measurements of the mission-planning software’s performance throughout development.
rationale: Requires recording and maintaining technical performance measurements but omits management measurements, establishment, reporting, and use.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall audit the ground-system monitoring software to confirm that each software component is the correct version and matches its configuration records.
rationale: Requires configuration audits for correct component versions and conformity to their records.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall review reported problems in the mission-planning application’s reused software components only when those problems are marked as high severity.
rationale: Explicitly limits assessments of reused-component problems to high severity, contradicting mandatory assessment of all reported nonconformances.

requirement_text: When tailoring of an NPR 7150.2D requirement is approved, the NASA Project Manager shall document and reflect that tailored requirement in the plans or procedures controlling development, acquisition, and deployment of the affected flight-control software.
rationale: Identifies approved directive tailoring rather than ordinary software-product changes, and records it in controlling plans or procedures.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall identify cybersecurity risks in the mission-planning software and list ways to reduce them, but will not create a plan for putting those protections in place.
rationale: Explicitly rejects planning mitigation implementation, a mandatory action, despite identifying risks and mitigations.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall test the ground-control software cybersecurity mitigation implementations required by the security vulnerabilities and weaknesses analysis, and shall record the test results.
rationale: Both tests and records results for the required mitigations derived from the specified analysis.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall review the ground-control software’s test results and save a written evaluation of what the results show.
rationale: Requires evaluation of test results and recording the evaluation.

requirement_text: When flight software requirements change, the NASA Project Manager shall update its test plans, but may retain test procedures even when those procedures are inconsistent with the changed requirements.
gap_type: Procedures may remain inconsistent with changed requirements
rationale: Expressly allows inconsistent procedures, contradicting the required consistency of plans and procedures.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall test the mission-planning software on a desktop computer before delivery, without testing it on its intended operating system or a high-fidelity simulation.
gap_type: Missing validation on the target platform or high-fidelity simulation
rationale: Explicitly excludes the targeted operating system and high-fidelity simulation and therefore waives the required target-platform or simulation validation.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall identify and record risks affecting the mission communication software, analyze them, and create plans to reduce them, but does not need to track the risks or share the plans with the project team.
rationale: Explicitly waives tracking and communicating risks and plans. Control is also missing. These direct waivers take precedence over the positive recording, analysis, and planning actions.

requirement_text: The NASA Project Manager shall keep a record of changes to the satellite communication software but does not need to evaluate how those changes affect the software.
rationale: Explicitly waives evaluation of software-product changes, despite requiring change records.

requirement_text: Before retiring the mission-planning software, the NASA Project Manager shall identify which records and software tools need to be archived, where they will be stored, and how the team can access them later.
rationale: Requires identification of archive contents, location, and access procedures for retirement.
